knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says to summarise completed work, exclusions, limitations and client decisions in factual language, and to send records only through approved channels.
Work that cannot be completed safely is escalated, and items without evidence are not marked complete. Client decisions are recorded, not left unrecorded.
The detailed method says to summarise what was completed, what was excluded, any damage or access limitations, and what requires client decision.

practicalCriteria: Reports accurately, protects privacy and links improvement to measured reinspection outcomes.
Uses the authorised work order and site instructions
Recognises and escalates hazards or scope limitations
Records objective evidence and correction where needed
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 2: Summarise what was completed, what was excluded, and any damage or access limits.
Record of procedure step 3: List the client decisions still needed, and state them in clear, factual language without promising a result that has not been verified.
Record of procedure step 7: Check at the next inspection whether the improvement worked, and record facts rather than assumptions.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Confirm the actual work scope, the hazards, and who can authorise any change before you start.
Stop work if procedure step 8 is not done: Stop and seek direction when work is unsafe, outside your training, or in conflict with a site instruction.
